explain.say: Sing, goddess, of the anger of Achilles. With an appeal like that, Homer's Iliad begins, nearly three thousand years ago. An epic is a long poem about heroes whose deeds shape a whole people. The timeline shows epics around the world, from Mesopotamia and India to Mali and Milton's England.

explain.say: Sort the conventions, the habits epics share. They open by calling on the muse, a goddess of poetry, and plunge in medias res, Latin for into the middle of things. Their style uses epic similes, long comparisons, and epithets like swift-footed Achilles. And the hero often visits the underworld. Which have you seen in films?

Look at the map. In Virgil's Aeneid, written for the emperor Augustus, the Trojan Aeneas flees burning Troy, falls in love with Queen Dido at Carthage, then leaves her at the gods' command and sails for Italy, where his descendants will found Rome. Duty beats love. What does an epic like this do for an empire?

draw.label: Aeneas’s voyage in Virgil’s Aeneid: from burning Troy, via Carthage, to Italy, where Rome will rise

explain.say: Here is a useful contrast from the critic C. S. Lewis. On the left, primary epic, composed to be sung aloud, like Homer and Beowulf. On the right, secondary epic, written by learned poets who imitate it, like Virgil and Milton. Milton keeps the muse and a war in heaven, but makes true heroism patience and faith. Why change what heroism means?

After Milton, full epics grew rare, and writers began to play with the form: Alexander Pope turned a stolen lock of hair into a mock Trojan War, and in 1990 Derek Walcott gave the epic to Caribbean fishermen. Superb. Challenge: tell your journey to school as an epic, with an invocation and one epic simile.

faq.q: What are the conventions of epic?
faq.a: Common features include an invocation of the muse, a statement of theme, beginning in medias res, a hero of great importance, gods who intervene, epic similes, epithets, catalogues of warriors or ships, and a journey to the underworld.

faq.q: What does in medias res mean?
faq.a: Latin for into the middle of things. Epics often begin partway through the story, then fill in the past through flashbacks, as the Odyssey and Paradise Lost do.

An extended comparison, often running for several lines, that compares a hero or event to something from everyday life or nature, such as an army to falling leaves. It is also called a Homeric simile.

The ancient Greek poet traditionally credited with the Iliad and the Odyssey, probably composed in the eighth or seventh century BCE from a long oral tradition. Whether he was one person is still debated.

faq.q: Why is Paradise Lost an epic?
faq.a: Milton uses every epic convention: an invocation of the muse, beginning in medias res with Satan in hell, a war in heaven, epic similes and catalogues. But his subject is the fall of all humankind, so he claims to surpass Homer and Virgil.

facts: The Iliad and the Odyssey are usually dated to the eighth or seventh century BCE.
Virgil left the Aeneid unfinished when he died in 19 BCE.
Paradise Lost was first published in 1667 in ten books, and revised into twelve in 1674.
